symptom: `ON ERROR CONTINUE` on a retrieve did nothing: the clause parsed, exec reported no error, and `describe microflow` showed the retrieve with no error handler (ako/CapTrackV3 FINDINGS §11). The mirror failure was live at the same time and unreported — CREATE and COMMIT *did* carry the clause, and mxbuild rejects Continue there: `$T = CREATE M.Thing (...) COMMIT ON ERROR CONTINUE` builds as CE6035 "Error handling type is not supported", with `mxcli check` passing.
cause: errorHandlingType is a property of Microflows$MicroflowAction, but the flow builder set it on the ActionActivity — a field sdk/microflows declares on BaseActivity, the metamodel does not have on an ActionActivity, and NEITHER engine serializes. Both writers instead emitted a hardcoded literal "Rollback" on the action (7 sites per engine). Fixed by adding ErrorHandlingType to RetrieveAction/DeleteObjectAction, setting it on the ACTION via a new explicitErrorHandling() that returns empty unless the author actually wrote a clause, carrying it in both writers (stringOrDefault/orDefault instead of the literal), reading it back in both parsers, and adding the two cases to getActionErrorHandlingType so DESCRIBE renders it. New rule MDL076 refuses Continue on create/commit.
insight: Mendix enforces a PER-ACTION-TYPE subset of one enum, which nothing in the metamodel or gen expresses — measured on 11.14.0 by writing each value into a stored document and building: Retrieve/Delete accept Rollback+Continue+Abort; MicroflowCall accepts Continue but not Abort; Log/Create/Change/Commit/Aggregate accept only Rollback. Two consequences that invert the obvious fix. (1) The hardcoded "Rollback" was LOAD-BEARING: a nanoflow's no-clause default is Abort, so serializing the builder's value unconditionally would have broken every nanoflow that logs or creates — hence carrying it only for an explicit clause. (2) A repo artifact encoded the wrong claim: 308-commit-on-error-rollback-roundtrip.mdl asserted `commit ... on error continue` 'must survive equally', and it does survive — into a model mxbuild refuses. Its Usage block ran exec + describe and never `mx check`, so a describe->exec->describe fixpoint was mistaken for a valid model; MDL076 is what surfaced it. A round-trip test proves fidelity, never validity. The measurement itself was VACUOUS on the first pass and only said so because the probe printed its own patch count: the Delete writer emits no ErrorHandlingType key, so setting it changed nothing and mxbuild's silence read as 'accepted' — the probe was changed to INSERT an absent key.
